provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original task, each object is a hollow V-shaped funnel. Its two diagonal arms run toward a 2x2 block. The output fills each funnel solid. For every non-background colour c and every row holding at least two c cells, the factory paints background cells between the outermost c cells. This matches the generator: each column's arm cell is filled upward to the top row, which gives the same horizontal spans. Bounding boxes cannot overlap, so a fill never crosses another object. Reflections (index >= 4, row reversal) do not change which axis the fill runs along. Rotating 90 or 270 degrees turns rows into columns. So for d4 % 4 in {1, 3} the emitted program fills along columns between the outermost same-coloured cells; otherwise it fills along rows. The background is the constant palette[0], since the generator's background is colour 0. Only background cells are overwritten.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the generator's domain: background is original colour 0, and every object has a distinct colour (as random_colors provides). If two separate objects shared a colour on the same line, they would be wrongly bridged. Demonstrations are not consulted. Rectangular grids are handled generically. No tests were run by me.
